A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ThinkVideo paper, with all 21 pages and Appendices A–H readable. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical research content; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its version-specific link differ.

before.justification: v1 reports original ThinkVideo benchmark results in Tables 1–5, ablations in Tables 6–7 and Figure 7, and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark, ablation, and qualitative results, including ThinkVideo-GPT-4o's 65.5 J&F on ReasonVOS in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same MLLM keyframe selection, Seg-Zero image segmentation, SAM2 propagation, mask postprocessing, and online keyframe-update procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MeViS, Refer-DAVIS-17, ReasonVOS, ReVOS, and T-ReasonVOS. The instance-segmentation and online demonstrations also retain identical task and scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Each comparison retains its original comparator set, including the VideoLISA and VISA variants in Tables 1–4 and ThinkFirst+SAM2 in Table 5. The qualitative comparison methods are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix D retain identical model configurations, keyframe sampling, evaluation metrics, and dataset sampling. T-ReasonVOS still contains 180 video-query pairs from 45 videos.

E4.justification: The keyframe-sampling and selector ablations in Tables 6–7, CoT ablation in Figure 7, and appendix examples, failure case, and ambiguity analysis are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and average runtimes, without disclosed repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical. ThinkVideo-GPT-4o retains J&F scores of 60.1 on MeViS, 65.5 on ReasonVOS, and 55.5 on T-ReasonVOS in Tables 1, 3, and 5.

T1.justification: The formal task definitions, mask non-overlap condition, and Equations (1)–(12) are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free CoT reasoning, segmentation performance, instance-level outputs, and the online extension.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations are identical, including dependence on pretrained MLLMs, failures to distinguish similar instances, ambiguous benchmark queries, and evaluation limitations discussed in Appendices F–G.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–D retain the same model versions, hyperparameters, prompts, hardware specifications, and dataset-selection details. The code link and planned code/data release statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are identical, including the positioning relative to VISA, VideoLISA, ThinkFirst, and Seg-Zero.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 24 May 2025 to v2 dated 28 June 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology, section structure, and appendices remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and A1–A7, Tables 1–7, captions, and body layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–21 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the arXiv stamp.

improvement.justification: v2 changes only the administrative arXiv stamp and its version link. The scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and research presentation are identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
